newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha peers into contango.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Naphtha peers into contango.

text.p: Naphtha in Singapore threatened to flip into contango on Wednesday amid weak demand, while high-octane gasoline was actively bid up on tight supplies, traders said.
Brokers said August swaps were unchanged from Tuesday at $21.40/$21.50 per barrel, but on par with September.
August on Tuesday was just two cents per barrel higher than September.
"The contango is coming back real fast," a trader said.
Prompt demand from Thailand which pushed the oversupplied market into backwardation about two weeks ago, has yet to resurface after the long weekend holiday in Thailand.
Some requirements were heard still uncovered but the buyer was sidelined in the softening market, traders said.
"The market is getting weaker and is in a downtrend," a South Korean trader said.
He said a South Korean petrochemical company was seeking first-half September supplies, but generally South Korea was at "tanktops" and some endusers trying to swap cargoes with Japanese buyers.
A Japanese trading house was also seeking a prompt cargo of MidEast naphtha specifications, but Thailand had absorbed the last spot availability of the grade.

In comparison, demand for high octane gasoline was rampant on the Singapore fob market with at least three buyers--two European majors and a Singapore trader--bidding the market up to $24.30 per barrel from $23.85 for August 7-12 cargoes of 97-octane grade.
Traders said supplies were tight, partially due to cuts in reforming capacity in the region and firm octane enhancer MTBE prices.
